    15  /-!
    16  # The coproduct (a.k.a. the free product) of groups or monoids
    17  
    18  Given an `ι`-indexed family `M` of monoids,
    19  we define their coproduct (a.k.a. free product) `Monoid.CoprodI M`.
    20  As usual, we use the suffix `I` for an indexed (co)product,
    21  leaving `Coprod` for the coproduct of two monoids.
    22  
    23  When `ι` and all `M i` have decidable equality,
    24  the free product bijects with the type `Monoid.CoprodI.Word M` of reduced words.
    25  This bijection is constructed
    26  by defining an action of `Monoid.CoprodI M` on `Monoid.CoprodI.Word M`.
    27  
    28  When `M i` are all groups, `Monoid.CoprodI M` is also a group
    29  (and the coproduct in the category of groups).
    30  
    31  ## Main definitions
    32  
    33  - `Monoid.CoprodI M`: the free product, defined as a quotient of a free monoid.
    34  - `Monoid.CoprodI.of {i} : M i →* Monoid.CoprodI M`.
    35  - `Monoid.CoprodI.lift : (∀ {i}, M i →* N) ≃ (Monoid.CoprodI M →* N)`: the universal property.
    36  - `Monoid.CoprodI.Word M`: the type of reduced words.
    37  - `Monoid.CoprodI.Word.equiv M : Monoid.CoprodI M ≃ word M`.
    38  - `Monoid.CoprodI.NeWord M i j`: an inductive description of non-empty words
    39    with first letter from `M i` and last letter from `M j`,
    40    together with an API (`singleton`, `append`, `head`, `tail`, `to_word`, `Prod`, `inv`).
    41    Used in the proof of the Ping-Pong-lemma.
    42  - `Monoid.CoprodI.lift_injective_of_ping_pong`: The Ping-Pong-lemma,
    43    proving injectivity of the `lift`. See the documentation of that theorem for more information.
    44  
    45  ## Remarks
    46  
    47  There are many answers to the question "what is the coproduct of a family `M` of monoids?",
    48  and they are all equivalent but not obviously equivalent.
    49  We provide two answers.
    50  The first, almost tautological answer is given by `Monoid.CoprodI M`,
    51  which is a quotient of the type of words in the alphabet `Σ i, M i`.
    52  It's straightforward to define and easy to prove its universal property.
    53  But this answer is not completely satisfactory,
    54  because it's difficult to tell when two elements `x y : Monoid.CoprodI M` are distinct
    55  since `Monoid.CoprodI M` is defined as a quotient.
